title: He didn’t wake up evil.
paragraphs: He became it… one choice at a time.
And that’s what should terrify you.

Because the red horse isn’t just coming for nations—
it rides through hearts.
But you don’t see where it started.

Not on a battlefield.
Not in a war room.
Not even in politics.

A wound.
An offense.
A pride that refused to bow.
And suddenly, peace didn’t stand a chance.
We think we’re far from this man.
We say, “I would never become that.”

How many times have you replayed an argument in your head—
wanting to win, not reconcile?

How many times have you let anger simmer…
until it felt justified?

How many times have you smiled outside,
but inside… you were already at war?
“Anyone who is angry with a brother or sister will be subject to judgment.” — Matthew 5:22
The red horse in Revelation isn’t just about global chaos.
It’s about the removal of peace.
“Its rider was given power to take peace from the earth and to make people kill each other…” — Revelation 6:4

Some scholars interpret this as literal warfare across nations.
Others see it also as the unraveling of human relationships—
violence breaking out because sin is no longer restrained.
But either way, the root is the same:
A heart that no longer submits to God.
You don’t need a sword to carry the spirit of the red horse.
Because war doesn’t always look like bloodshed.

Sometimes it looks like silence.
Cold shoulders.
Sharp words.
Secret hatred.
And God sees all of it.
“The heart is deceitful above all things and beyond cure.” — Jeremiah 17:9

That means you can convince yourself you’re right—
while your soul is slowly hardening.
Because while the red horse takes peace away…

When Jesus stood before His accusers,
He had every right to call down angels.
Every right to destroy His enemies.
Every right to end the war with power.
“He was oppressed and afflicted, yet He did not open His mouth…” — Isaiah 53:7
“The punishment that brought us peace was on Him…” — Isaiah 53:5

The peace you keep losing in your relationships…
the peace your heart keeps craving…
the peace the world cannot manufacture…
You are not just a victim of chaos.
You are a participant in sin.
“For all have sinned and fall short of the glory of God.” — Romans 3:23
But God didn’t leave you there.
“But God demonstrates His own love for us in this: While we were still sinners, Christ died for us.” — Romans 5:8
And He carried them to the cross.
Then He did what no rider, no king, no system could ever do.
“Therefore, since we have been justified through faith, we have peace with God through our Lord Jesus Christ.” — Romans 5:1
What are you doing with the war inside you?
Or are you ready to surrender it?

Because you cannot hold onto anger
and expect to walk in peace.

You cannot cling to pride
and expect to experience grace.

You cannot keep fighting everyone around you
and claim to follow the Prince of Peace.
“Blessed are the peacemakers, for they will be called children of God.” — Matthew 5:9
“If we confess our sins, He is faithful and just and will forgive us…” — 1 John 1:9
He’s not waiting to condemn you.
You don’t have to be ruled by rage.
You don’t have to keep losing peace.
You don’t have to become what you fear.
In Christ, you can become new.
“If anyone is in Christ, he is a new creation…” — 2 Corinthians 5:17
